name: lcdproc
desc: Display real-time system information on a LCD
why: Drives character LCD displays from system data, a charming old-school hardware hobby with a real physical payoff.

brief.what_it_is: LCDproc is an open source client/server suite that shows real-time system information on character LCD displays, running on Linux and *BSD. The server, LCDd, drives the display hardware, and clients such as lcdproc send it screens showing things like CPU load, system load, memory usage and uptime. The README says the server also accepts key or remote-control input for controlling the clients. The brew executable list also includes helper scripts such as fortune.pl, lcdmetar.pl, tail.pl and x11amp.pl.
brief.why_it_exists: The README describes LCDproc as a client/server suite with drivers for all kinds of LCD devices, so a small display can show a machine's status without a monitor. The original developer, William Ferrell, reflects in the README that it began as a small single-system utility for one device type and grew into a client/server daemon used around the world.
brief.how_it_works: Clients and the server talk over a TCP connection, so the client and the display do not have to be on the same machine. The README gives the example of a client in Sweden showing its stats on an LCD in the United States. The server handles the device driver side, with support for serial, USB and parallel-port displays.
brief.install_notes: The README defers installation to an INSTALL.md file in the archive, which covers how to connect an LCD to your system. I did not fetch that file, so I have no concrete build or configuration steps. You need a supported display (serial, USB or parallel-port) and the matching driver, and the server and client run as separate programs. The homepage's download section was not fetched.
brief.standout: The client/server split over TCP means a machine can show its stats on a display attached to a different machine, and the server supports a long list of LCD controllers from several vendors. Control input from the display back to the clients is also supported.
brief.status: quiet. The homepage's newest release news is v0.5.6, dated 2012-11-04, and its news list stops around 2012. The GitHub README includes a Travis CI badge and a copyright line running to 1998-2016, and it says the repository takes pull requests and has open issues. I could not see commit dates or a latest release tag, so recent activity is unconfirmed.
brief.caveats: The homepage and README list different device families; the homepage is an older site and its device list is less complete than the README's. The homepage's news and downloads point at 2012-era releases. The license is GPL v2 or later, as stated in the README. The brew description is the same one-liner as the project's own short description, and it does not mention the need for physical hardware, which the README makes clear. I did not check build requirements, which are in INSTALL.md.
quotes: LCDproc is a client/server suite including drivers for all kinds of nifty LCD devices.
it is possible to have a client on a box in Sweden showing its stats on a LCD device in the United States.
we focus on writing software and leave politics out of it.
